summary: Capitana is a bilingual playable lunar mission trainer about evidence, teamwork and connected systems. Players choose an avatar and a four-role crew, handle a fictional thruster fault, move solar panels into an illuminated zone, and plan five base systems: energy, air, food and water, radiation, and communication. Mistakes pause the mission for explanation, repair and retry, without death or rankings. A historical NASA DONKI solar-particle record becomes a learning checkpoint: players must separate an event timestamp and instrument channel from an unknown lunar dose. The game connects NASA resources with qualitative engineering choices, then asks players to explain how the systems support one another. English and Spanish, touch and keyboard controls, crew advice and a no-name mission postcard make the prototype easy to explore. It is educational fiction, not a validated engineering simulator, and its AI-assisted code, visuals, text and rule proposals are disclosed.
details:
CAPITANA: FIRST LUNAR BASE

B2Bytes: Diego Díaz and Lya Mundaca Acuña.

PLAY AND INSPECT

English: https://alfi-b2bytes.github.io/capitana-lunar-trainer/

Spanish: https://alfi-b2bytes.github.io/capitana-lunar-trainer/es.html

Code, sources and contribution history: https://github.com/alfi-b2bytes/capitana-lunar-trainer

HOW IT WORKS

A static HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with no sign-up or personal-data collection. Players choose an avatar and four crew roles, handle a fictional thruster fault, move solar panels and plan five base systems. Each incorrect choice opens explanation, repair and retry. Crew candidates have equal technical training and qualitative working styles, without hidden numerical bonuses. Four crew voices offer advice. A final learning check connects the systems; replay and a no-name SVG postcard support reflection.

NASA EVIDENCE

The radiation checkpoint uses NASA CCMC DONKI historical SEP event 2024-05-10T13:35:00-SEP-001, 10 May 2024 at 13:35 UTC, GOES-P SEISS >10 MeV, M2M_CATALOG v1. Players distinguish an event time and instrument channel from an unknown lunar dose. This is not live telemetry or a forecast. NASA references support illumination, CO2 removal, plant growth, radiation protection and relay planning.

INTERACTION AND ACCESS

English and Spanish are selectable. Panels support drag, touch and keyboard placement. The base lights up under an explicitly fictional rule requiring both panels in the illuminated zone, not a calculation of real power, consumption or illumination. Storage is a separate planning choice. Reduced-motion support and repair without death or rankings aim to make exploration welcoming.

AI CONTRIBUTIONS AND AUTHORSHIP

The supplied brief records human educational goals and narrative constraints, and marks some material as uncertain in origin. AI generated implementation code, SVG illustrations, the fictional adult Capitana Planeta guide, names, explanatory text, translations and presentation; AI assisted source checks and testing. AI also proposed specific rules and gameplay improvements, including the five-turn structure, evidence checkpoint and solar interaction. Diego approved the initial rules and selected the solar interaction; approval does not change their AI origin. NASA observations are cited source data, not AI-generated measurements. Visuals and the postcard have visible AI labels; code/data use is disclosed in metadata and documentation. No NASA endorsement is claimed.

TESTING AND LIMITS

Six complete production paths in English/Spanish at 320, 390 and 1440 CSS pixels passed, including ten incorrect-choice retries, DONKI interpretation, crew advice, sources and completion. Drag, keyboard placement and the solar completion gate were checked. No JavaScript errors were observed. These are functional tests, not child usability studies. No learning outcomes have been measured. This is a qualitative educational prototype, not a validated engineering simulator. AI-ideation eligibility remains subject to the organizers' interpretation; clarification was requested.

LICENSE

Original application code: Apache License 2.0. NASA references retain their own terms. Generated illustrations and no-name interface symbols are not NASA branding. No identifiable minors are represented. Third-party PDF font notices are listed among other resources.
